chunks: 3548 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Regarding the apostate from Islam, he عليه السلام said: "She is not to be killed, but is to be subjected to hard service, prevented from food and drink except what keeps her alive, dressed in the coarsest clothes, and struck for the prayers."

key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion from which apostasy occurred
key_terms.الْمُرْتَدِّ: the apostate; one who turns back from Islam
key_terms.تُسْتَخْدَمُ: she is made to serve or put to labor

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the ruling on a female apostate in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a female apostate from Islam, outlining punitive and coercive measures rather than execution. It also indicates the continued obligation of salat (prayer) upon her within the legal framework described.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3548 - Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a person who apostasizes from Islam:
"He is not to be killed but is to be subjected to hard labor, denied food and drink except what sustains his life, made to wear coarse clothing, and beaten to perform prayers."
